newsitem.title: UK: UK expects to exceed Rio target for CO2 emissions.
newsitem.headline: UK expects to exceed Rio target for CO2 emissions.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it will cut ozone-threatening gases even further by the turn of the century than it promised at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.
Environment minister John Gummer said he expected Britain's emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2), the main greenhouse gas, to be between four and eight percent below 1990 levels by the year 2,000.
He said emissions of methane would be 22 percent below 1990 levels and those of nitrous oxide would be down 62 percent.
The Rio convention called on developed countries to cut their emissions of greenhouse gases back to 1990 levels by the year 2,000.
Few other developed countries were doing as well, said Gummer. Nevertheless, he said he would propose new, tough targets at a meeting of European Union environment ministers next month.
"I have proposed that developed countries reduce emissions of all greenhouse gases to between five and 10 percent below 1990 levels by 2010," Gummer said in a statement.
"(It is a) challenging target for some of the world's largest emitters, but one which can be achieved if all take their commitments as seriously as the United Kingdom."

Gummer attributed the expected fall in Britain's greenhouse gas emissions to a number of factors, including the privatisation of the energy sector, which led many electricity generators to switch from oil or coal to gas and to improvements in the nuclear industry.
He also said campaigns encouraging the public to use energy more efficiently and increases in fuel duties had contributed to the expected reduction.
